harvest-stats/auth-me-no-retry-after-fai.sentence: After GET /api/auth/me fails on /login, there is no way to retry without a page reload.
harvest-stats/auth-me-no-retry-after-fai.evidence: With the browser cookies cleared, I routed GET **/api/auth/me to return a 500 and opened http://localhost:3790/login. The console showed /api/auth/me returning 500 and the normal Sign in form appeared. It worked: the email and password fields and the Sign in button were all there, because loadCurrentUser() (composables/useAuth.ts) catches the error and returns null, so the middleware just treats the visitor as not signed in. I removed the route, filled in the DEMO credentials and clicked Sign in on the same page, with no reload. POST /auth/login succeeded and the app went to the Dashboard (/). Any later navigation also runs the global middleware again and calls /auth/me again while the user is null. So the user can recover without reloading: the sign-in form is the way forward. The other failure modes in the report (400, connection reset, 429) go through the same catch-all, so they behave the same way. login.vue, useAuth.ts and auth.global.ts are not touched by the diff, so this is not a regression from the stats change.

harvest-stats/dashboard-nan-on-malformed.sentence: When GET /api/tasks/upcoming returns malformed JSON, the dashboard renders the text 'NaN'.
harvest-stats/dashboard-nan-on-malformed.evidence: Signed in as the demo user. Used Playwright browser_route to make GET **/api/tasks/upcoming* return a 200 application/json response with the truncated body '{"id": 1, "title": "broken'. The first full load is rendered on the server, so the browser route doesn't apply and the page looked normal. I then went to /plants and clicked the Dashboard nav link, which makes the browser send GET /api/tasks/upcoming?limit=5 itself (confirmed in performance entries). The 'Upcoming tasks' section then showed 26 rows reading '– · Due in NaN days' instead of an error message. The unparseable body is kept as a string (26 characters), and index.vue's `v-for="task in tasks"` (guarded only by `tasks && tasks.length`) makes one TaskItem per character, each with no due date, so the due calculation gives NaN. The dashboard tasks code is unchanged in this diff, so this is probably pre-existing, but it happens on the dashboard and users would not accept it.

harvest-stats/dashboard-summary-no-retry.sentence: After GET /api/dashboard/summary fails on the dashboard, there is no way to retry without a page reload.
harvest-stats/dashboard-summary-no-retry.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, opened /plants, then used Playwright page.route to fail GET /api/dashboard/summary and went to the Dashboard with a client-side link click. (A first page load is rendered on the server, so browser_route can't touch it.) One 500 never shows an error: ofetch's built-in GET retry sent a second request (n=2) and the summary cards loaded normally. When I failed it with 400 once, 500 twice or 429 twice, the summary section showed only the AlertMessage text ('Server exploded') with no button or link in it, so the report is right that there is no retry control. But a reload isn't the only way out: clicking Plants and then Dashboard in the nav fetched again and showed the full summary every time. The error branch in index.vue (`<AlertMessage v-if="summaryError">`) is the same on main; the change only edited the top-plant StatCard hint and link. AlertMessage has no retry option, and no page in the app (tasks, beds, plants/[id]) has a retry button for a failed load. This is the app's existing error pattern, which this change neither added nor touched, and the request asked for nothing here. The claim that only a reload helps is also false, because going to another page and back recovers.

harvest-stats/dashboard-tasks-no-retry-a.sentence: After GET /api/tasks/upcoming fails on the dashboard, there is no way to retry without a page reload.
harvest-stats/dashboard-tasks-no-retry-a.evidence: I added a Playwright route that makes GET **/api/tasks/upcoming* return 500 {"detail":"boom"}, then signed in as demo@example.com. The client-side navigation to / then rendered the 'Upcoming tasks' section with only an alert reading 'boom'. There was no Retry/Try again button, and the summary cards loaded normally. I then removed the route so the API was healthy again and clicked the 'Dashboard' nav link while on /. The section still showed the 'boom' alert and no tasks, so the only way to recover is a full page reload. The code agrees: in frontend/app/pages/index.vue tasksError renders a bare <AlertMessage> with no action, and refreshTasks is only called after a task toggle, which is impossible while the list is not shown. AlertMessage.vue is just a slot, and no page in frontend/app has a retry control. Note: this code is unchanged from main, so the defect predates the harvest-stats change rather than being introduced by it. There is a workaround (reload), so severity is low.

harvest-stats/dashboard-undefined-on-mal.sentence: When GET /api/dashboard/summary returns malformed JSON, the dashboard renders the text 'undefined'.
harvest-stats/dashboard-undefined-on-mal.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /plants. Used a Playwright route to make GET /api/dashboard/summary return 200 application/json with the truncated body '{"plant_count": 3, '. Then clicked the Dashboard link to navigate to / on the client. ofetch/destr treats the unparsable body as a plain string, so `summary` is a non-empty string, the v-else-if='summary' branch renders, and every field is undefined. The dashboard showed 'In undefined beds', 'HARVESTED IN UNDEFINED' and 'undefined harvests', with an empty Plants value. No error message appeared. Caveat: this text comes from the Plants and Harvested cards in frontend/app/pages/index.vue, which `git diff main` shows were not changed. The only dashboard card the change touched, 'Top plant this year', handled the bad data and showed 'None yet' / 'By harvest weight'. So the defect is real and visible on the changed page, but it existed before this change and only appears when the server sends a broken response.

harvest-stats/delete-bed-control-stays-d.sentence: In automated fault-injection runs, after a failure or reload on various pages, navigating to /beds leaves a DeleteBed control disabled for more than 10 seconds.
harvest-stats/delete-bed-control-stays-d.evidence: beds.vue is not touched by the change. Its Delete button is bound to :disabled="deletingId === bed.id || bed.plant_count > 0" with title 'Move or delete its plants first'. In the browser I signed in, opened /stats, reloaded it, then went to /beds and waited 11 s. The Delete buttons for 'North bed' (2 plants) and 'Shade corner' (1 plant) stayed disabled, and each showed the tooltip 'Move or delete its plants first'. I then created an empty bed through the API and reloaded /beds. Its Delete button was enabled immediately, so the button is not stuck on loading after a reload or failure. It is disabled on purpose, with the reason shown, for beds that still contain plants. The fault-injection runs create plants and beds, which explains why they saw disabled Delete buttons. The temporary bed was deleted afterwards (HTTP 204).

harvest-stats/login-no-retry-after-failu.sentence: After POST /api/auth/login fails (500, reset, 400, 429), retrying from /login does not reach the Dashboard without a page reload.
harvest-stats/login-no-retry-after-failu.evidence: Using Playwright, I made the first POST /api/auth/login fail and let the second go through to the real API. I tried a 500 with a JSON detail, a 500 with a plain-text body, a connection reset, a 400 and a 429. Each failure showed an error alert on /login ('fail 500', 'The garden server could not be reached.' and so on). I then entered the credentials again and clicked Sign in on the same page, with no reload. All five times the second request was sent (route count 2), the page went to / and the 'Dashboard' heading appeared within 10 s. On failure, the login page deliberately clears the password field (pages/login.vue). If you click Sign in again without re-typing it, you get 'Enter your email and password.' rather than a hang. Once the password is typed again, it reaches the Dashboard. The change does not touch login.vue, useAuth or useApi.

harvest-stats/stats-best-plants-long-tex.sentence: A plant with a long unbroken name or variety overflows the Best plants cards on /stats at 375 px, causing sideways page scrolling.
harvest-stats/stats-best-plants-long-tex.evidence: Via the API I created a plant named 'Supercalifragilisticexpialidociousheirloomtomato' with an 80-character variety that has no spaces ('Extremelylongvarietynamewithoutanyspaces' x2, the schema maximum), then logged a 999,999 g harvest on 2026-11-01 so it ranked No. 1. I signed in through Playwright and opened /stats at 375x800. document.documentElement.scrollWidth was 618 against a 375 viewport, and window.scrollTo(200,0) moved the page to scrollX=200, so the page really scrolls sideways. The first Best plants card (li.stat, width 343) has p.stat__hint with scrollWidth 574 against clientWidth 290. In the full-page screenshot the variety text runs well past the right edge of the card and the viewport. p.stat__value (the plant name) does not cause it: it has overflow:hidden, nowrap and an ellipsis, and showed 'Supercalifragilis…'. The cause is in main.css: .stat__hint has only margin, font-size and color, with no overflow-wrap, word-break or min-width rule. The table is fine because it scrolls inside its own .table-scroll wrapper. The variety field accepts 80 characters (schemas.py PlantIn), so ordinary input can trigger this. I deleted the test plant afterwards.

harvest-stats/stats-cleared-date-silent-.sentence: Clearing the From or To field on /stats drops it from the query and the server silently uses the current-year bound, so the blank input disagrees with the range used and can yield a confusing 'From must be on or before To' error.
harvest-stats/stats-cleared-date-silent-.evidence: Signed in as demo user, opened /stats (initial: '5 harvests from 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2026'). Cleared the From input with Playwright fill(''): the input stayed blank, the request went out as GET /api/stats/harvests?to=2026-12-31 with no 'from', the result text still said 'from 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2026', and the 'This year' reset button appeared even though the data shown was this year's. Then I set To to 2025-12-31 with From still blank: the request was ?to=2025-12-31, the page showed the error 'The From date must be on or before the To date.' while From looked empty, and no results appeared. Code matches: stats.vue's query computed leaves out empty values, and stats.py replaces a missing from/to with year_bounds(today.year). The visible inputs disagree with the range the server actually uses, and the user gets a misleading validation error.

harvest-stats/stats-date-fields-ignore-u.sentence: On /stats the From/To fields are read from the URL only at setup, so pressing Back or clicking the Stats nav link changes the URL but leaves the old range shown.
harvest-stats/stats-date-fields-ignore-u.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /stats. Set From to 2026-03-01. The URL became /stats?from=2026-03-01 and the page read '5 harvests from 1 Mar 2026 to 31 Dec 2026'. Then I clicked the 'Stats' link in the main nav. The URL changed to /stats with no query, which is the default this-year range, but the From field still said 2026-03-01 and the results still read '5 harvests from 1 Mar 2026 to 31 Dec 2026'. So the URL and the page disagree. Code agrees: stats.vue sets dateFrom/dateTo from route.query only once at setup, and the only watch goes from the refs to the URL (router.replace). Nothing watches route.query, so when the URL changes while the component stays mounted, the fields are never updated. I only tested the nav-link path. Because the page uses router.replace, Back usually leaves /stats, but the same root cause applies to any in-page URL change.

harvest-stats/stats-empty-months-omitted.sentence: The /stats per-month table only has columns for months that have harvests, so months in the chosen range with no harvests are missing rather than shown as zero.
harvest-stats/stats-empty-months-omitted.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /stats with the default range 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31. The table header was 'Plant | Jun 2026 | Jul 2026 | Aug 2026 | Sept 2026 | Total', so Jan-May and Oct-Dec 2026 have no columns. The API agrees: GET /api/stats/harvests with the default range returns months ['2026-06','2026-07','2026-08','2026-09'], and from=2025-01-01&to=2026-12-31 returns ['2025-08','2026-06','2026-07','2026-08','2026-09'], jumping from Aug 2025 to Jun 2026. Cause: backend/routers/stats.py builds `months = sorted({row['month'] for row in rows})`, using only months that have harvest rows instead of every month in the From-To range. The page shows no note saying empty months are left out, so a 'per month for a chosen date range' table that hides empty months misleads the reader about gaps and seasonality. Totals are still correct.

harvest-stats/stats-malformed-200-not-ha.sentence: When GET /api/stats/harvests returns a malformed or non-JSON 200 response (e.g. '{}' or an HTML body), /stats throws a render error or shows a garbage table instead of an error state.
harvest-stats/stats-malformed-200-not-ha.evidence: Signed in as demo user, loaded Dashboard, then used Playwright page.route to fulfil GET /api/stats/harvests with 200 (a) application/json '{}' and (b) text/html '<html>proxy</html>', and clicked the 'Stats' nav link. In both cases the URL changed to /stats but the Dashboard content stayed on screen (title 'Dashboard · Garden Log'), a Nuxt error dialog appeared with h1 "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')", the console logged '[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of render function at <Stats>', and a pageerror 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')' was thrown. No AlertMessage or retry was shown. Cause: stats.vue's template checks `stats && stats.plants.length` with no validation of the response shape (useApiFetch treats any 200 as data), and formatMonth calls value.slice without a null guard.

harvest-stats/stats-no-request-timeout.sentence: useApiFetch sets no timeout, so if GET /api/stats/harvests hangs, /stats shows 'Loading stats…' (or blocks navigation to Stats) indefinitely instead of failing after 10 seconds.
harvest-stats/stats-no-request-timeout.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: signed in as the demo user, opened /stats (it loaded 5 harvests and the table), then used page.route('**/stats/harvests**') with a handler that never responds and changed To to 2026-06-30. One request went out (GET /api/stats/harvests?from=2026-01-01&to=2026-06-30). After 3 s and again after 15 s the page showed 'Loading stats…' with no error, and the old table and best plants stayed on screen (the table was not removed, unlike sample report 1). But this isn't a defect of this change. The request doesn't mention a timeout, and nothing in the repo specifies one: grep finds no 'timeout' anywhere in frontend/app or nuxt.config. composables/useApi.ts (useApiFetch/useApiClient) is untouched by the diff (git diff main shows no change to composables), so every existing page fetches the same way with no timeout. stats.vue does use the project's shared fetch wrapper as intended and does have an error state (AlertMessage on statsError), which shows if the request fails. The '10 seconds' expectation comes from the reports, not from the request or the codebase.

harvest-stats/stats-no-retry-after-error.sentence: When the stats request fails, /stats offers no Retry control, so the user must change a date or reload the page to refetch the same range after the server recovers.
harvest-stats/stats-no-retry-after-error.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: signed in as the demo user, opened /stats, made GET **/api/stats/harvests** return 500 with a text/plain body using a Playwright route, then changed From to 2026-02-01. The page showed 'Could not load harvest stats.' and the only buttons were 'Sign out' and 'This year'. After removing the route, the page stayed on the error until the date changed or the page was reloaded. But the request never asks for a Retry control, and the page does have a clear error state (AlertMessage with role=alert), so report 2's claim that there is 'no error state' and the page keeps saying 'no harvests' is wrong. This also matches how the rest of the app works: grep finds no Retry control anywhere in the frontend. The dashboard's summary and tasks errors (index.vue:61,96), the beds load error (beds.vue:151) and tasks.vue all show the same AlertMessage with no retry button. Stats follows the existing pattern, and changing the range or reloading recovers. A missing Retry button is a possible enhancement for the whole app, not a defect in this change.

harvest-stats/stats-null-fields-rendered.sentence: When GET /api/stats/harvests returns null fields in a 200 response, /stats renders text such as 'null harvests from – to –' and a nameless table row.
harvest-stats/stats-null-fields-rendered.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, used Playwright to route GET /api/stats/harvests to a 200 response with harvest_count, date_from, date_to, months, top_plants and total_grams set to null, and plants:[{plant_id:1, plant_name:null, variety:null, total_grams:null, monthly_grams:null}], then opened /stats. The page showed 'null harvests from – to –', an empty Best plants list, and a table row with no plant name. So the reported behaviour does happen. But this response breaks the API's own contract. The endpoint declares response_model=HarvestStatsOut, and in backend/schemas.py every one of these fields is non-optional (int, date, list[...], str), so FastAPI/pydantic will not send a 200 response with these nulls. The frontend type HarvestStats declares them as non-null too. The rest of the app, which existed before this change, trusts its typed API responses the same way: the dashboard, plant detail and beds pages all pass server counts straight to plural() without checking for null. The output only appears when an impossible server response is faked. The request does not ask for client-side validation of responses, and a real user cannot reach this state, so it is not a defect in the change.

harvest-stats/stats-partial-date-typing-.sentence: Typing a year digit by digit in a /stats date input fires a request per keystroke, and intermediate dates earlier than From flash a 422 validation error.
harvest-stats/stats-partial-date-typing-.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /stats (From 2026-01-01, To 2026-12-31). Clicked the To input, moved to the year segment and typed 2026 one digit at a time, 250ms apart, in Chromium. Four GET /api/stats/harvests requests went out: to=0002-12-31, 0020-12-31 and 0202-12-31 each came back 422, and only to=2026-12-31 came back 200. While I was typing, the page showed the alert 'The From date must be on or before the To date.' in place of the table, and the console logged 3 errors. Code cause: in stats.vue the useFetch query is a computed built straight from the v-model refs, with no debounce and no check that from <= to or that the year is plausible. The backend returns 422 when from > to. Typing a date is a normal way to use the page, and the spec expects a working date-range filter, so flashing an error on every half-typed year is not acceptable behaviour.

harvest-stats/stats-raw-validation-messa.sentence: Opening /stats with an impossible but well-formed date such as ?from=2026-02-30 shows a raw 'Query.from: Input should be a valid date...' message and a blank From field, because queryDate() only checks the regex.
harvest-stats/stats-raw-validation-messa.evidence: Signed in as the demo user in Playwright and opened http://localhost:3792/stats?from=2026-02-30. inputValue('#stats-from') was '' (the browser rejects the impossible date). The page showed only the raw API error 'Query.from: Input should be a valid date or datetime, day value is outside expected range', with no table. Code: frontend/app/pages/stats.vue:13-14 queryDate() only checks /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/, so the bad value is sent to the API, which returns a 422 that is shown with its technical loc prefix. The user sees an empty From field next to a technical error, and gets no fallback to the default.

harvest-stats/stats-signed-out-reload-re.sentence: After a signed-out reload of /stats, a request is still in flight after 10 seconds.
harvest-stats/stats-signed-out-reload-re.evidence: With cookies cleared, I loaded /stats (it redirects to /login?redirect=/stats), let it reach network idle, reloaded, and tracked every request the reload started for 10.5 s. I did this 3 times for /stats and 3 times for /tasks (an unchanged page as a baseline). Every request finished every time; nothing was in flight. The 'pending' requests only appeared when goto was immediately followed by reload. Those were requests from the first load that the reload cut off: Vite /_nuxt/ dev modules, and once /api/auth/me. Playwright never fires finished/failed events for them, and the same thing happened on /tasks, which this change doesn't touch. So it's a measurement artifact, not a hanging request. Called directly with no session, the API answers at once: /api/stats/harvests returns 401 in 25 ms and /api/auth/me returns 200 in 4 ms. Signed out, the auth middleware redirects before stats.vue runs its fetch.

harvest-stats/stats-table-long-plant-nam.sentence: A long unbroken plant name in the /stats table's nowrap row header pushes all weight columns out of view at 375 px.
harvest-stats/stats-table-long-plant-nam.evidence: Via API (demo user) created plant 'Supercalifragilistic'x4 (80 chars, no spaces, the max allowed by PlantIn) in bed 1 and logged a 99,999 g harvest on 2026-10-01. Opened /stats at 375x800. The CSS added in the change sets `.stats-table th[scope=row] { white-space: nowrap }`. Measured: the row header is 542 px wide, but the .table-scroll container shows only 309 px (right edge at x=342). The first month column (Jun 2026) starts at x=575 and Total at x=997. The table's scrollWidth is 1043 px, while the document scrollWidth stays at 375, so the page does not scroll sideways but the table does. An element screenshot of the table shows only the PLANT column (Courgette, Lettuce, the long name clipped, Tomato, Total) and not one weight value. This applies to every row, so none of the weights can be read without scrolling the table sideways. In Best plants, .stat__value has text-overflow: ellipsis and overflow: hidden (scrollWidth 1144 vs clientWidth 290) with no title attribute, so the full name is cut off there too (the link has a visually hidden full name for screen readers only).

plant-journal/beds-delete-stays-disabled.sentence: After an injected failure on various requests (plants, beds, journal), an automated check navigating to /beds finds the DeleteBed control still disabled after 10 s (some runs also report the bed Name field emptied after a failed GET /api/beds).
plant-journal/beds-delete-stays-disabled.evidence: beds.vue is not touched by the change (git diff main has no beds files). Its Delete button is bound to :disabled="deletingId === bed.id || bed.plant_count > 0" and shows the title 'Move or delete its plants first'. The backend also returns 409 for deleting a bed that still has plants. The live data has two beds, North bed (2 plants) and Shade corner (1 plant). In the browser, after injecting a 500 on GET /api/plants/1 and then going to /beds, both Delete buttons were disabled with that tooltip, so it is a deliberate guard with the reason shown, not a stuck busy state. I added an empty bed 'Verify empty bed': its Delete worked through the confirm dialog and removed the bed (checked through the API). The 'Name' field being empty is just the blank 'Add a bed' form, which starts empty. A failed GET /api/beds did not wipe any entered data (with server-side rendering the page still showed the beds). The DeleteBed ids in the reports (3z8839iz etc.) look like beds the checker created that contained plants.

plant-journal/edit-refresh-failure-hides.sentence: On the plant detail page, if the list refresh after a successful entry edit fails, the whole journal list disappears and only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, ignoring the PUT response.
plant-journal/edit-refresh-failure-hides.evidence: Signed in as demo, opened /plants/1 (2 journal entries shown in .journal-list). Clicked Edit on the first entry, used Playwright route to make GET /api/journal?plant_id=1 fail, changed the text and clicked 'Save entry'. PUT /api/journal/2 returned 200, then the refetch GET failed. Afterwards .journal-list was gone (count 0). With an aborted request the section showed only 'Could not load the journal.'; with a 500 it showed only the server detail. No retry button appeared, and the badge still said '2 entries'. A direct API GET then confirmed the edit had been saved (body 'Edited again VERIFY-456'). Code: [id].vue onEntrySaved ignores the emitted updated entry and only calls refreshJournal(); the failed useFetch refresh clears data, so the v-if on the list hides every entry.

plant-journal/edited-marker-same-second.sentence: An entry edited within the same second it was created is not marked 'edited' because created_at and updated_at have one-second resolution and compare equal.
plant-journal/edited-marker-same-second.evidence: Through the API: POST /api/journal (plant 2) returned entry 4 with created_at = updated_at = '2026-11-12 13:30:14'. A PUT straight after it changed the body to 'same-second test EDITED', but updated_at stayed '2026-11-12 13:30:14' because SQLite datetime('now') only has 1-second resolution. On /plants/2 in the browser, that entry showed the changed text with no 'edited' marker (JournalEntryItem.vue:20 compares updated_at !== created_at). Control: editing the same entry again through the UI more than a second later made the 'edited' marker appear (1 .journal-entry__edited element). So whether an edit is marked depends on timing: a real edit made in the same second is shown as never edited.

plant-journal/entry-limit-counts-utf16.sentence: The JournalEntryForm textarea maxlength and character counter count UTF-16 code units, so emoji count double, only about 250 emoji fit, and existing server-accepted emoji entries cannot be re-saved when edited.
plant-journal/entry-limit-counts-utf16.evidence: Server (JournalEntryIn.body max_length=500) counts code points: POST /api/journal with 500x🌱 -> 201, 501x🌱 -> 422. JournalEntryForm.vue uses :maxlength=500, remaining = 500 - form.body.length and validate() checks form.body.trim().length (all UTF-16 units). In the running app on /plants/2, filling the New entry textarea with 300 🌱 left only 250 emoji in it (value.length 500, 250 code points) and the hint said '0 characters left'. Clicking Edit on the API-created 500x🌱 entry showed the hint '-500 characters left'; clicking Save entry without changing anything showed 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.' and the save was blocked. So a valid, server-accepted entry cannot be re-saved, and emoji input is capped at half the limit the request specifies. Test entry deleted afterwards.

plant-journal/future-date-timezone-misma.sentence: The no-future-date check compares against the server's date.today() while the form uses the browser's local date, so a user in a time zone ahead of the server can have today's entry rejected as a future date.
plant-journal/future-date-timezone-misma.evidence: The server's local clock reads Thu 2026-11-12 14:24 CET. Code: schemas.JournalEntryIn.not_in_future compares against date.today(), the server's local date. JournalEntryForm takes its default and max from todayIso(), the browser's local date. I opened a Playwright browser context with timezoneId 'Pacific/Auckland', where the browser's time was Fri 2026-11-13 02:26 GMT+13. I signed in as the demo user and went to /plants/2 (Courgette). The journal date input defaulted to 2026-11-13 with max=2026-11-13, so the client accepts it as today. I typed text and clicked 'Add entry' without changing the date. POST /api/journal {entry_on:'2026-11-13', body:'TZ test entry today', plant_id:2} came back 422 'Value error, Journal date cannot be in the future.' and the entry was not saved. So with the default date (the user's own today), the add-entry form is refused for users whose local date is ahead of the server's. The edit path (PUT) uses the same validator.

plant-journal/journal-add-retry-duplicat.sentence: Retrying 'Add entry' after a POST /api/journal whose response was lost or timed out creates a duplicate entry because the endpoint has no idempotency key or dedupe.
plant-journal/journal-add-retry-duplicat.evidence: Reproduced the mechanics through the API: two identical POST /api/journal requests (plant 1, same date and body) created two rows (ids 4 and 5). Both were listed, and I deleted them afterwards. create_entry in backend/routers/journal.py inserts without any idempotency key, but this matches the existing app: plants, beds, tasks and harvests all insert unconditionally too (I checked that a plain POST /api/tasks also just creates a row with 201). The client does not retry on its own: useApi.ts uses $fetch/ofetch, which does not retry POSTs by default, so a duplicate only happens when the user deliberately submits again after the 'The garden server could not be reached.' error. The request asks for add/edit/delete/list/search/counts and says nothing about idempotency or exactly-once delivery. A second entry after a lost response is the normal at-least-once behaviour of a plain REST create; the gardener can see it in the list and delete it. A retried DELETE returning 'not found' is the same thing. Neither is a regression, and the request does not require either to behave differently.

plant-journal/journal-ancient-date-accep.sentence: POST/PUT /api/journal accepts implausible past dates such as 0001-01-01 (201 Created) with no lower bound, showing them as '1 Jan 1' at the bottom of the list.
plant-journal/journal-ancient-date-accep.evidence: Reproduced: logged in via API and POST /api/journal {plant_id:1, entry_on:'0001-01-01'} returned 201 and stored the entry. However, the request only asks for 'dated journal entries' and specifies no lower date bound. The implementation (JournalEntryIn.not_in_future in backend/schemas.py) deliberately mirrors the pre-existing, unchanged harvest validation (HarvestIn.not_in_future): I confirmed POST /api/harvests with harvested_on 0001-01-01 also returns 201 on main's existing code. Accepting old dates and rejecting only future dates is the app's established convention, and an entry dated year 1 sorting last in a newest-first list is correct ordering. Test data was deleted afterwards (journal 4, harvest 7).

plant-journal/journal-bad-response-shown.sentence: When GET /api/journal returns 200 with a non-list body, the Journal page shows '0 entries' and the 'No journal entries yet' empty state instead of an error.
plant-journal/journal-bad-response-shown.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and landed on the dashboard. Used Playwright browser_route to make **/api/journal?** return 200 application/json {"detail":"weird"}, then clicked the Journal nav link (client-side navigation). The main text read: 'Journal / ... / 0 entries / No journal entries yet / Open a plant and write the first entry in its journal. / Go to plants'. No error alert appeared. Code confirms it: pages/journal.vue only shows AlertMessage when useFetch's `error` is set. The template checks `entries && entries.length`, which is falsy for an object, so it falls through to the `v-else-if="entries"` empty state. resultText uses `entries.value?.length ?? 0`, which gives '0 entries'. Nothing checks that the response is an array, so a broken response looks like a real empty journal.

plant-journal/journal-body-nul-500.sentence: POST or PUT /api/journal with a body starting with a NUL character returns 500 because SQLite length() fails the CHECK constraint and the IntegrityError is unhandled.
plant-journal/journal-body-nul-500.evidence: Logged in as the demo user through the API. POST /api/journal {"entry_on":"2025-01-01","body":"\u0000x","plant_id":1} returned 'Internal Server Error' [500]. PUT /api/journal/5 with body "\u0000abc" also returned 500. Control cases: 'nul\u0000x' and 'ok' both returned 201. Code check: JournalEntryIn.body only has min_length=1/max_length=500, so Pydantic accepts the value. db.py has CHECK (length(body) BETWEEN 1 AND 500), and SQLite's length() on TEXT stops at the first NUL, so it returns 0 and the INSERT/UPDATE fails. routers/journal.py does not catch sqlite3.IntegrityError, so the client gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx validation error. I deleted the test entries afterwards.

plant-journal/journal-delete-retry-404.sentence: Retrying a journal entry delete after the first DELETE succeeded server-side (lost response or another tab) returns 404 and the plant page shows 'Journal entry not found.' while the stale entry stays listed.
plant-journal/journal-delete-retry-404.evidence: API: signed in as demo user, created journal entry 4, DELETE /api/journal/4 -> 204, repeat DELETE -> 404 {"detail":"Journal entry not found."} (delete_entry calls _get_entry first, which raises 404). Browser: opened /plants/2 with entry 'STALE-ENTRY-XYZ' shown, deleted it server-side with a separate fetch (simulating another tab or a lost response), then clicked the entry's Delete button in the page and accepted the confirm. The page showed 'Journal entry not found.' and the deleted entry stayed in the list, because removeEntry in pages/plants/[id].vue only calls refreshPlantAndJournal on success and has no 404-as-done handling. Note: harvest delete in the original code behaves the same way, so this follows an existing pattern. The error text is accurate and a reload clears the stale entry, so impact is small.

plant-journal/journal-feed-long-name-ove.sentence: On /journal at 375 px width, a long unbroken plant name in .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap and pushes the page into horizontal scrolling.
plant-journal/journal-feed-long-name-ove.evidence: Via the API (signed in as the demo user) I created a plant named 'W'x80. PlantIn allows max_length=80, so the API accepted it. I added a journal entry for it, then opened /journal in Playwright at a 375x800 viewport. document.documentElement.scrollWidth was 1568 against a clientWidth of 375, and the A.journal-feed__plant link for the long name reached right=1551px. Its computed overflow-wrap and word-break were both 'normal'. In main.css, overflow-wrap:anywhere is set only on .journal-entry__body; .journal-feed__plant has neither overflow-wrap nor word-break. So the page scrolls sideways on mobile when a plant name is valid but long. (The exact numbers differ from the reports because 'W' is a wide glyph.) I deleted the test plant afterwards.

plant-journal/journal-huge-id-500.sentence: Sending an integer id larger than 64 bits as plant_id or entry id to POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /api/journal returns 500 Internal Server Error from SQLite overflow instead of a 4xx.
plant-journal/journal-huge-id-500.evidence: Signed in via POST /api/auth/login with DEMO credentials (200), then used curl against the running API. With ids 99999999999999999999 and 9223372036854775808 (2^63): POST /api/journal {plant_id:<big>,entry_on:'2026-01-01',body:'x'} -> 500 'Internal Server Error'; PUT /api/journal/<big> -> 500; DELETE /api/journal/<big> -> 500; GET /api/journal?plant_id=<big> -> 500. Control: DELETE /api/journal/9223372036854775807 (max int64) -> 404 'Journal entry not found.' Code: routers/journal.py has unbounded int path params, and JournalEntryCreate.plant_id / the plant_id query only check gt=0, so Python ints that don't fit in 64 bits reach sqlite3, which raises OverflowError, and nothing handles it. The same thing already happens in existing endpoints (GET /api/plants/<big>, POST /api/harvests, DELETE /api/harvests/<big> all return 500), so this is an existing app-wide pattern that the new journal endpoints copy and add to. It only happens with crafted API input that the UI never sends, and no data is changed or exposed.

plant-journal/journal-load-error-no-retr.sentence: When GET /api/journal fails, the /journal page and the plant detail Journal section show only 'Could not load the journal.' with no Retry control, so recovery requires a reload or changing the search.
plant-journal/journal-load-error-no-retr.evidence: Reproduced: signed in as the demo user, routed **/api/journal* to a 500 in Playwright, then went to /journal and to /plants/2 by clicking links in the app. Both showed only an alert ('boom', the API's detail; it falls back to 'Could not load the journal.') with no Retry button. The plant badge read '0 entries' because the plant data is from before the mock, not a count of the failed list. Code agrees: journal.vue:69 and plants/[id].vue:306 render a bare <AlertMessage>. But this is the app's existing convention. On main, every load-error state is a bare AlertMessage with no retry: plants list ('Could not load plants.'), beds ('Could not load beds.'), dashboard summary and tasks, plant detail ('Could not load this plant.') and the harvest form's plant list. No page in the original app has a retry control (git grep for retry/'try again' finds only the login error text). The request does not ask for retry on load errors. The new journal views match the established design, so a missing Retry is a feature request, not a regression or a gap against the request. (The report that a search with an apostrophe makes the API fail would be a separate issue and was not judged here.)

plant-journal/journal-requests-no-timeou.sentence: Journal requests have no client timeout, so when the API hangs the add/save/delete buttons stay disabled on 'Saving…' or the list stays on 'Loading entries…' indefinitely instead of failing after 10 s.
plant-journal/journal-requests-no-timeou.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: signed in as the demo user, opened /plants/1 (Tomato), used Playwright to route non-GET /api/journal requests so they never get a response, typed an entry and clicked 'Add entry'. 15 s later the button still read 'Saving… [disabled]' and no alert was shown. So the behaviour is real. But it is not a defect introduced by this change and nothing asked for a timeout. (1) The request text says nothing about timeouts or a 10 s limit. The '10 s' expectation in the reports is made up. (2) The journal code uses the app's existing useApiClient/useApiFetch from composables/useApi.ts. That file is unchanged from main (`git diff main -- frontend/app/composables` is empty). No file in frontend or backend contains a timeout or AbortSignal. Every existing feature (auth, beds, harvests/new, index, plants/new, plants/[id], tasks) calls the same client with no timeout, so a hung API leaves their buttons in the same busy state. The journal follows the app's established request convention, and when a request does fail, its errors are caught and shown. Leaving out a client timeout is an app-wide design choice, not a fault in the journal feature. Side note: while I tried a comparison test with a hung harvest delete, the Playwright MCP accepted a confirm dialog, and one demo harvest (600 g on 3 Aug 2026, Tomato) was deleted.

plant-journal/journal-search-ignores-url.sentence: On /journal the search box is initialised from route.query.q only once, so browser Back/Forward or in-app URL changes leave the search box and results out of sync with the URL.
plant-journal/journal-search-ignores-url.evidence: Code: pages/journal.vue reads route.query.q once and syncs search->URL with router.replace (one direction only). I ran this in the browser as demo user. Steps: Dashboard -> Journal (3 entries) -> search 'Courgette' (URL ?q=Courgette, 0 match) -> 'Tomato' (URL ?q=Tomato, 2 match) -> Back went to the Dashboard (router.replace does not add a history entry per search, so there is no stale journal state to step back into) -> Forward came back to /journal?q=Tomato with box 'Tomato' and 2 matching results, all in sync because the page remounts. So the reported Back/Forward desync did not happen. The one desync I could cause: on /journal?q=Tomato, clicking the 'Journal' nav link changes the URL to /journal, but the box still says 'Tomato' and the list stays filtered. The Plants list page, which was already in the initial commit (main:pages/plants/index.vue), uses the exact same pattern (ref initialised once from route.query + watch -> router.replace). It shows the same behaviour: /plants?q=Tomato -> click 'Plants' nav -> URL /plants, box still 'Tomato'. The journal page follows the app's existing URL-sync convention for search filters, and the request asked for nothing beyond a search box. The reported Back/Forward problem did not reproduce, and the remaining nav-link quirk is existing app-wide design, not a regression from this change.

plant-journal/journal-stale-count-on-err.sentence: On /journal, when a later search request fails, the previous results count still shows above the load error because the count does not check loadError.
plant-journal/journal-stale-count-on-err.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and loaded /journal. The results count showed '3 entries'. I then routed **/api/journal** to fail and typed in the search box, once with an HTTP 500 response (detail 'boom') and once with a network abort (search 'to', then cleared back to empty). Each time the error alert appeared ('boom' / 'Could not load the journal.') and the .results-count paragraph was empty (innerHTML '<!--v-if-->'). No stale count showed. The template does not check loadError, but Nuxt 4's useFetch resets data to its default (undefined) when a request fails, so the v-else-if="entries" branch does not render. The claimed symptom does not occur.

plant-journal/plant-journal-capped-at-50.sentence: The plant detail page fetches journal entries with limit=500 and no paging, so a plant with more than 500 entries shows only the newest 500 while the badge shows the full count.
plant-journal/plant-journal-capped-at-50.evidence: Code: frontend/app/pages/plants/[id].vue:15 calls useApiFetch('/journal', {query:{plant_id, limit: 500}}); backend/routers/journal.py caps limit at le=500 (limit=600 returns 422) and has no offset/cursor, and the page has no paging or 'more' control. Reproduced: signed in as the demo user through the API, added 520 dated entries ('Bulk entry 1..520') to plant 2 (Courgette). GET /api/plants/2 gave journal_count=520; GET /api/journal?plant_id=2&limit=500 returned 500 rows. In the browser, /plants/2 showed the badge '520 entries' but exactly 500 <li> items in .journal-list. The last one was 'Bulk entry 500' (30 Jun 2025), there was no more/older/next button, and the 20 oldest entries could not be seen, edited or deleted from the plant page, with nothing telling the user the list was cut short. plant-journal/plants-list-no-retry.sentence: On /plants, after GET /api/plants fails with 500, there is no way to retry loading without reloading the page.
plant-journal/plants-list-no-retry.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, used browser_route to make GET /api/plants (with and without query) return 500, then went to /plants with the nav link. The page showed the header, the filters and an error alert reading 'boom', with no Retry button. So the missing button is real. But the change doesn't cause it. `git diff main -- frontend/app/pages/plants/index.vue` adds only the journal-count badge on each card. The error branch (`AlertMessage v-if=plantsError`, no refresh) is the same as in the initial commit, and no page in the app has a retry button (grep finds no 'retry' or 'Try again'). The request doesn't ask for one either. Changing the search or bed filter refetches too, because the query is reactive. This is the app's existing error-handling pattern, not a defect in this change. The third sample report ('Basil ${unique}' not visible) looks like a broken placeholder in the test script, not app behaviour.

plant-journal/search-like-wildcards-unes.sentence: Searching the journal for '%' or '_' returns all entries because the term is used as an unescaped SQL LIKE pattern, so literal % or _ cannot be searched.
plant-journal/search-like-wildcards-unes.evidence: Signed in via POST /api/auth/login with the demo credentials, then called GET http://localhost:8792/api/journal with different q values. q='' returned 3 entries, and none of them contains '%' or '_' in its body. q='%' returned all 3, q='_' returned all 3, q='%%%' returned all 3, and a control q='zzqx' returned 0. So searching for a literal % or _ matches everything. Code: backend/routers/journal.py list_entries builds the clause as f"(j.body LIKE '%{term}%' OR p.name LIKE '%{term}%')", which is raw interpolation with no escaping and no ESCAPE clause. The existing escape_like helper in routers/common.py, which plants.py uses, is not used here. The same interpolation also opens the query to SQL injection (term is not bound as a parameter).

plant-journal/search-non-ascii-case-sens.sentence: Journal search is case-sensitive for non-ASCII letters (e.g. 'épinards' does not match 'ÉPINARDS') because SQLite LIKE folds only ASCII case.
plant-journal/search-non-ascii-case-sens.evidence: Through the API (signed in as the demo user), I created a journal entry on plant 2 (Courgette) with the text 'Été chaud, ÉPINARDS rrcheck' (id 4). GET /api/journal?q=épinards returned nothing, and so did q=été. q=ÉPINARDS and q=Épinards both returned the entry. The ASCII part of the text matched in either case: q=rrcheck and q=RRCHECK both returned it. In the code, backend/routers/journal.py list_entries filters with plain `j.body LIKE ? OR p.name LIKE ?`. There is no lower()/casefold and no custom collation, and SQLite's LIKE only ignores case for ASCII letters. The /journal page (frontend/app/pages/journal.vue) sends the search box text straight to the server as ?q= and filters nothing on the client, so the search box behaves the same way. Searching therefore ignores case for ASCII letters but not for accented ones, which is inconsistent. I deleted the test entry afterwards.

plant-journal/search-over-80-raw-error.sentence: Typing more than 80 characters into the /journal search box (which has no maxlength) makes the API return 422 and the page replace results with a raw 'String should have at most 80 characters' message.
plant-journal/search-over-80-raw-error.evidence: Signed in as demo user, opened /journal, filled the Search input (#journal-search) with 81 'a' characters. Input accepted all 81 chars (maxlength attribute is null). After the request, the <main> text was: 'Journal ... Search / Clear search / Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters' — the entries list was replaced by the raw Pydantic validation message, with a console error from the failed request. Code agrees: backend/routers/journal.py declares q: str = Query(default="", max_length=80), and frontend/app/pages/journal.vue sends the trimmed search value with no length limit and shows apiErrorMessage(loadError) in place of results. The user is not told the limit in plain words and cannot see any results until they shorten the text.

watering-log/add-bed-stuck-after-malform.sentence: On /beds, when GET /api/beds returns malformed JSON, a render error is thrown and the 'Add bed' button stays disabled on 'Adding…'.
watering-log/add-bed-stuck-after-malform.evidence: Signed in as the demo user (via POST /api/auth/login in the Playwright context), opened /beds and let it load normally. Then I routed GET /api/beds so it returns 200 application/json with the truncated body '{"oops": [1,2,'. I typed a bed name and clicked 'Add bed'. The POST went through, and the refresh() GET (1 intercepted request) got the malformed body. ofetch could not parse it, so beds.value became a raw string. The totalPlants computed (beds.value?.reduce) then threw 'beds.value?.reduce is not a function' as an uncaught pageerror, with console warnings '[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of render function' and '... of component update'. The component stopped re-rendering, so after 10 s the submit button still showed 'Adding…' and was disabled: adding=false was set in the finally block but never got rendered. The page stays frozen until reload and no error message is shown. Note: the code that throws (totalPlants, and the template's beds.length / v-for with no shape check) is not new in this diff. The beds page as changed still hits the problem, though, and nothing guards against a non-array response.

watering-log/ancient-date-accepted.sentence: A past watering dated far in the past (e.g. 0001-01-01) is accepted by the form and POST /api/waterings and listed as '1 Jan 1'.
watering-log/ancient-date-accepted.evidence: Reproduced via API: POST /api/waterings {bed_id:1, watered_on:'0001-01-01', litres:1} returned 201 (id 3), then deleted. Code: WateringIn only rejects future dates (not_in_future); beds.vue date input sets only :max=today. However this exactly mirrors the pre-existing app convention on main: HarvestIn.harvested_on has the same future-only validator and no lower bound, and POST /api/harvests with harvested_on 0001-01-01 is also accepted with 201 (created id 7, deleted). The request asks only for recording a past watering with a date; it sets no lower bound. 0001-01-01 is a valid ISO date and '1 Jan 1' is the correct rendering of it by the en-GB formatter (UTC, no shift), so the display is accurate, not corrupted. Accepting an implausible but valid user-typed past date is consistent with the app's established design rather than a regression or a broken requirement.

watering-log/auth-me-error-no-retry.sentence: On /login, when GET /api/auth/me fails (500, 400, reset, 429), there is no way to retry without a page reload.
watering-log/auth-me-error-no-retry.evidence: On /login the global middleware calls loadCurrentUser() (composables/useAuth.ts), which catches any GET /api/auth/me error and returns null. The page then shows the normal sign-in form. This code is unchanged by the watering diff. In Playwright, for each of 500, 400, connection reset and 429 I made the first /api/auth/me request fail, cleared cookies, and loaded /login. Each time the sign-in form appeared and nothing was stuck. Without reloading, I entered the demo credentials and submitted, and each time I reached the Dashboard (URL /, title 'Dashboard · Garden Log', 'Recent waterings' table shown). The middleware also calls /auth/me again on the next navigation, so the call is retried anyway. On the login page a failed session check just means 'not signed in', and submitting the form is the way forward. No dedicated retry button is needed, and none is in scope for the watering request.

watering-log/bed-filter-not-synced-with-.sentence: On /waterings, the bed filter is read from the URL only at setup, so navigating to /waterings or using back/forward keeps the old filter while the URL changes.
watering-log/bed-filter-not-synced-with-.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and clicked North bed's history link on /beds (/waterings?bed=1): the select showed '1' and the list showed '1 watering, 10 L in total' (North bed only). Then I clicked the 'Waterings' nav link. The URL became /waterings, but the select stayed on '1' and the list still showed only North bed's 1 watering. Back (to ?bed=1) and Forward (to /waterings) changed only the URL; the filter and list stayed the same. A full page load of /waterings showed the correct unfiltered list: All beds, '2 waterings, 14 L in total' (Shade corner + North bed). Cause in the code: pages/waterings.vue sets bedFilter = ref(route.query.bed) once at setup and only has watch(bedFilter) -> router.replace. Nothing watches route.query, and NuxtPage has no key, so the page component is reused. So the 'Waterings' nav link and Back/Forward leave the user on a filtered list that doesn't match the URL.

watering-log/beds-load-failure-clears-ty.sentence: On /beds, when GET /api/beds fails, the text typed into the Add bed 'Name' field is cleared and the retry does not recover.
watering-log/beds-load-failure-clears-ty.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /beds, which is server-rendered, so the first GET /api/beds the browser can intercept is the refresh after a POST. (1) Typed a name, clicked Add bed, made the first browser GET /api/beds return 500: the POST succeeded, the name field cleared, Nuxt useFetch retried the GET on its own and it succeeded, and the new bed's heading and 'Record past watering for <name>' button were visible within 1.5 s. The API list contained the bed. (2) Made every GET /api/beds return 500, typed a name, then clicked 'Water now' so the list refresh failed: the typed Name value was kept and the error alert was shown. (3) With every GET failing, submitted Add bed: the field cleared only because the POST had saved the bed, and after the failure was lifted a reload showed the bed. The field is cleared only after a successful save (Object.assign(newBed, emptyBed()) runs after the POST resolves), and that Add bed code is the same as on main. A failed load does not wipe typed values, and both the automatic retry and a reload recovered. The reporters' scripts most likely re-searched for a name that had been saved and then cleared, or used the unexpanded placeholder 'Bed ${unique}', which explains the 'not found' steps.

watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-after-b.sentence: On /beds, when GET /api/beds returns malformed JSON or hangs, an unhandled render error and dev error overlay appear.
watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-after-b.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened the dashboard. watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-bad-lit.sentence: On /beds, entering a negative value into the 'Litres' field triggers the dev error overlay.

No pageerror events, no console errors, no vite/nuxt error overlay element, and the page title stayed 'Beds · Garden Log'. In the code, savePastWatering (frontend/app/pages/beds.vue:122-131) rejects empty, non-finite and <= 0 values before any request. The backend schema (litres gt=0) also rejects them: POST /api/waterings with litres -5 returned a 422 validation error, not a crash.

watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-bed-pos.sentence: On /beds, when POST /api/beds hangs, the dev error overlay appears.
watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-bed-pos.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /beds. Using Playwright routing I made POST /api/beds (Add bed) (1) hang forever: after 20s the button just read 'Adding…', with no pageerror, no console error, and no custom elements such as nuxt/vite error overlays in the DOM; (2) hang for 8s and then abort as timed out: the page showed the inline alert 'The garden server could not be reached.', the only console output was the browser's own 'Failed to load resource: net::ERR_TIMED_OUT', no pageerror and no overlay; (3) hang, then click 'Water now', go to the waterings page and come back: no pageerror and no overlay. watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-on-navi.sentence: Reloading /beds or navigating back and forward to /beds triggers the dev error overlay.
watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-on-navi.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and went through the reported steps in the running app, watching for pageerror events, console errors and Vue warnings. (1) Reloaded /beds with a bed whose last watering was a past date-only entry: no errors, no overlay. The only way I got an uncaught error ('value.replace is not a function' in formatDateTime) was by injecting a numeric last_watered_at, which the API schema (str | None) never sends. That is not a realistic scenario and does not match the reports.

watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-waterin.sentence: On /beds, when POST /api/waterings hangs, the dev error overlay appears.
watering-log/beds-uncaught-error-waterin.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /beds. Routed POST /api/waterings so it never got a response, then clicked 'Water now' on North bed and waited 20s. The button stayed disabled showing 'Watering…'.
