There was no uncaught error and no overlay. The code matches this: recordWatering in beds.vue wraps api() in try/catch/finally and turns the error into the inline message with apiErrorMessage.

watering-log/boolean-litres-accepted.sentence: POST /api/waterings with litres set to boolean true is accepted with 201 and stored as 1.0 litres.
watering-log/boolean-litres-accepted.evidence: Signed in as the demo user via POST /api/auth/login, then sent POST /api/waterings {"bed_id":1,"litres":true}. The API returned 201 with {"id":3,"bed_id":1,"bed_name":"North bed","watered_on":"2026-11-12",...,"litres":1.0}, and GET /api/waterings then listed that row as a stored 1.0 L watering. With litres:false the same request got 422 (greater_than 0), which shows the boolean is being turned into a number rather than rejected as the wrong type. Cause: WateringIn.litres is declared as `float | None` in Pydantic lax mode (backend/schemas.py:131) with no strict typing, so true is coerced to 1.0. A boolean is not a valid amount in litres, so the API should reject it with 422; instead it stores made-up data. The UI form does not send booleans, so only direct API clients can trigger this.

watering-log/dashboard-nan-after-malform.sentence: On /, when GET /api/tasks/upcoming returns malformed JSON, the page shows the text 'NaN'.
watering-log/dashboard-nan-after-malform.evidence: Signed in as the demo user in Playwright, then routed GET **/api/tasks/upcoming** to return status 200, application/json, with the truncated body '{"id": 1, "title": "broken'. Then went client-side from /beds to / via the Dashboard link. The 'Upcoming tasks' card showed 26 rows of '– · Due in NaN days' (main text contained 'NaN'). Cause: ofetch/destr cannot parse the body, so it falls back to the raw string. pages/index.vue then checks `tasks && tasks.length`, which is truthy for the string, so `v-for` renders one TaskItem per character. For each row, dueLabel(undefined) -> daysUntil gives NaN. No error state is shown. Note: this code path is not touched by the watering change. The Upcoming tasks section, TaskItem.vue and useApi.ts are the same as in main, so this defect already existed rather than being caused by the change. The new Recent waterings section was not involved.

watering-log/dashboard-summary-error-no-.sentence: On /, when GET /api/dashboard/summary fails (500, 400, reset, 429), there is no way to retry without a page reload.
watering-log/dashboard-summary-error-no-.evidence: Signed in as demo user, routed GET **/api/dashboard/summary to 500 {"detail":"boom"}, navigated client-side /beds -> Dashboard. The Summary region showed only an alert 'boom' with no retry button or link (AlertMessage has just a slot; index.vue renders only the message when summaryError is set). After removing the route the alert stayed, with no refetch on focus or anything else; the only ways to recover are reloading, navigating away and back, or toggling a task (completeTask calls refreshSummary as a side effect). Grep finds no retry control anywhere in the app, and the summary error block is unchanged from main, so this is an existing gap that the change kept (the new Recent waterings section also has no retry). It is real but low impact: the other sections still render and navigating away and back recovers.

watering-log/dashboard-uncaught-error-ta.sentence: On /, when GET /api/tasks/upcoming is rate limited with 429, the dev error overlay appears.
watering-log/dashboard-uncaught-error-ta.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and used Playwright to return 429 for GET /api/tasks/upcoming, then went to / with client-side navigation (Beds -> Dashboard) so the browser made the request itself (a full reload fetches during SSR, where the browser route does not apply). I tried four cases: (1) 429 with JSON body {detail:'Too many requests'}: the Upcoming tasks section showed the alert 'Too many requests'; (2) 429 with a text/plain body: alert 'Could not load upcoming tasks.'; (3) 429 on tasks together with 401 on /api/dashboard/summary, the combination the report mentions: both sections showed inline alerts; (4) 429 with an empty body: alert 'Could not load upcoming tasks.'. In every case the dashboard rendered, the recent-waterings table still loaded, there was no vite/nuxt error-overlay element in the DOM, and the console held only 'Failed to load resource' network messages, no uncaught exceptions. The code agrees: index.vue reads tasksError from useFetch and shows it through apiErrorMessage, which guards every property it reads. The change did not touch the tasks fetch.

watering-log/dashboard-undefined-after-m.sentence: On /, when GET /api/dashboard/summary returns malformed JSON, the page shows the text 'undefined'.
watering-log/dashboard-undefined-after-m.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /beds. I then used page.route to make GET /api/dashboard/summary return status 200, content-type application/json, with the malformed body '{"plant_count": 3, broken', and clicked the Dashboard link (client-side navigation). The / page showed the stat cards as 'In undefined beds', 'HARVESTED IN UNDEFINED' and 'undefined harvests' instead of the 'Could not load the summary.' alert. Cause: when JSON parsing fails, ofetch falls back to the raw text string, so useFetch puts that string in data with no error. index.vue checks `v-else-if="summary"` (the string is truthy) and then reads summary.bed_count, summary.year and so on, which are undefined. Note: per git diff, this summary block in index.vue is unchanged from main. The watering change only added the Recent waterings section, which still rendered fine. So the defect is real and visible on /, but it was already there before this change. Severity is low because it only happens when the server sends a malformed response.

watering-log/dashboard-waterings-no-load.sentence: The dashboard 'Recent waterings' section shows only its heading with no loading indicator while GET /api/waterings is pending.
watering-log/dashboard-waterings-no-load.evidence: index.vue does useApiFetch('/waterings') (a thin wrapper over useFetch, not lazy) inside a top-level `await Promise.all([...])` in <script setup>, so Nuxt holds route navigation until the request settles; the dashboard never renders with waterings pending. In the browser, signed in as the demo user on /beds, I routed **/api/waterings* with a 6s delay and clicked the Dashboard nav link. At 0.5s, 2s and 4s the old Beds page (h1 'Beds') was still shown and no 'Recent waterings' section was in the DOM. At about 8s the dashboard rendered with the section already filled in (5 Nov 2026 Shade corner 4 L; 1 Nov 2026 North bed 10 L). A full page load is server-side rendered and also waits for the data. Nothing calls refresh() on the waterings fetch, so it never goes back to pending after the page is shown. The heading-only blank state described in the report never appeared. The template does lack a pending branch, but that branch could never be reached.

watering-log/delete-already-deleted-show.sentence: Deleting a watering that was already deleted (second tab or retry) on /waterings shows a 404 'Watering not found.' error and leaves the stale row.
watering-log/delete-already-deleted-show.evidence: Reproduced: created watering id 3 (North bed, 20 Oct 2026, 3 L) via the API, opened /waterings in the browser (3 rows), deleted id 3 directly via DELETE /api/waterings/3 (204), then clicked its Delete in the stale page and confirmed. The second DELETE returned 404 {"detail":"Watering not found."}; the page showed 'Watering not found.' and the row stayed until reload, because removeWatering only calls refresh() on success. However, this is the app's existing, uniform convention, not something this change introduced: delete_task, delete_harvest, delete_plant and delete_bed all look up the row first and raise not_found (404), and tasks.vue/beds.vue use the same try { DELETE; refresh() } catch { show error } pattern. The request never mentions deleting waterings, let alone idempotent deletes. The message is accurate and a reload fixes the list. Making delete idempotent would be a reasonable improvement, but it's an app-wide design choice rather than a defect in this change.

watering-log/huge-litres-breaks-layout.sentence: A stored extreme litres value such as -1e308 renders as a 300+ digit amount on /waterings and the dashboard, forcing horizontal scrolling at 375 px.
watering-log/huge-litres-breaks-layout.evidence: WateringIn.litres has only le=10_000 and no lower bound (backend/schemas.py), so POST /api/waterings {bed_id:1, litres:-1e308} returned 201 with litres -1e+308. formatLitres renders it via toLocaleString with no compacting. At a 375x800 viewport in the signed-in app: dashboard Recent waterings Amount cell is 414 chars ('-100,000,000,000,...'), documentElement scrollWidth=3380 vs clientWidth=375; /waterings Amount cell 414 chars, scrollWidth=3466 vs clientWidth=375 — forced horizontal scrolling. Negative amounts are not a sensible watering amount and the API accepts them. Test record deleted afterwards.

watering-log/invalid-bed-query-raw-error.sentence: Opening /waterings?bed=abc (or an unknown bed id) shows the raw validation text 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer...' or a blank filter selection.
watering-log/invalid-bed-query-raw-error.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /waterings?bed=abc. The page body shows the raw Pydantic/FastAPI text 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer' in the alert. The bed select value is '' (it displays 'All beds') while a 'Clear filter' button is shown, so the filter control does not match the filter in use. The SSR HTML fetched for /waterings?bed=abc contains role="alert" with that same text. The cause is in waterings.vue: the raw ?bed= value is passed as bed_id without any check, and the backend's 422 detail is shown as-is. /waterings?bed=999 shows '0 waterings / No waterings for this bed'. The select is again '' and shows 'All beds', which contradicts the message. The page never says the bed does not exist.

watering-log/login-error-no-retry.sentence: On /login, after POST /api/auth/login fails (500, reset, 400, 429), a retry does not reach the Dashboard within 10 s.
watering-log/login-error-no-retry.evidence: In Playwright I made the first POST /api/auth/login fail as 500, connection reset, 400 and 429, one run each, with later calls passing through. Every time the form showed an error ('err 500', 'The garden server could not be reached.', etc.) and the password field was emptied, because login.vue sets password.value = '' in its catch block. Clicking Sign in again right away sent no request. It only showed 'Enter your email and password.', which is why the reported retry never reached the Dashboard. When I typed the password again and clicked Sign in, the second request succeeded and the Dashboard heading appeared in all four cases. The button is re-enabled, so the user can retry without reloading. Emptying the password after a failed sign-in is a common, deliberate choice. login.vue, useAuth and useApi are not part of the watering change (git diff main does not touch them).

watering-log/long-bed-name-overflow-375.sentence: A bed with a long unbroken name makes the waterings tables on /waterings and the dashboard overflow horizontally at 375 px width.
watering-log/long-bed-name-overflow-375.evidence: Signed in as the demo user with a 375x800 viewport. Through the API I created a bed with a 60-character name containing no spaces (60 is the maximum the schema allows), got 201, then recorded a watering for it (201). On /waterings, document.documentElement.scrollWidth was 846 and the table was 813 px wide. Hiding that one row brought scrollWidth back to 375. On the dashboard, the Recent waterings table was 728 px wide and scrollWidth was 761; hiding the row brought it back to 375. The code agrees: the new tables in waterings.vue and index.vue print bed_name in a plain <td>, the .table td rules in main.css have no overflow-wrap or word-break, and there is no scroll wrapper. A name the app accepts makes both new pages scroll sideways on a phone. I deleted the test bed afterwards.

watering-log/non-finite-litres-500.sentence: POST /api/waterings with a non-finite litres value such as 1e400 (infinity) or NaN returns a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 422.
watering-log/non-finite-litres-500.evidence: Logged in via POST /api/auth/login with the demo credentials, then sent POST /api/waterings with curl. {"bed_id":1,"litres":1e400}, {"bed_id":1,"litres":NaN}, Infinity and -Infinity all returned HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error'. For comparison, litres 20000, "inf" and "nan" (as strings) returned a proper 422 'Input should be less than or equal to 10000'. No rows were inserted (GET /api/waterings still lists 2 entries, litres 4.0 and 10.0), so data is safe. The likely cause is that FastAPI's 422 response echoes the rejected input, and a non-finite float can't be JSON-encoded. WateringIn.litres (schemas.py:131) is a plain float with gt=0, le=10000 and no allow_inf_nan=False. Other endpoints that take floats seem to fail the same way: a quick POST /api/beds with area_m2 1e400 also returned 500. But the new endpoint does return a 500 instead of a validation error for invalid input.

watering-log/oversized-integer-id-500.sentence: Sending a bed_id or watering id above 64 bits (e.g. 99999999999999999999) to POST/GET/DELETE /api/waterings returns a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 4xx.
watering-log/oversized-integer-id-500.evidence: Signed in via POST /api/auth/login as the demo user, then used curl against the running API. POST /api/waterings {"bed_id":99999999999999999999,"litres":1} -> 500 'Internal Server Error'; GET /api/waterings?bed_id=99999999999999999999 -> 500; DELETE /api/waterings/99999999999999999999 -> 500; POST with bed_id 9223372036854775808 (2^63) -> 500. For comparison, in-range bed_id 999999 -> 422 {"detail":"Choose an existing bed."} and GET ?bed_id=999999 -> 200 []. Code: WateringIn.bed_id is Field(gt=0) and the query/path params are plain int with no upper bound, so Python ints above the 64-bit limit reach sqlite3, which raises OverflowError, and nothing handles it. Only the API is affected; the UI never sends such ids.

watering-log/requests-no-timeout.sentence: Watering requests (Water now, Save watering, waterings list, delete, dashboard) have no 10 s timeout, so a hanging API leaves 'Watering…'/'Saving…'/'Loading waterings…' on screen indefinitely.
watering-log/requests-no-timeout.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: signed in as the demo user, opened /beds, used Playwright page.route to hang every request whose URL contains 'water' (never answered), clicked 'Water now' on North bed. After 15 s the button still read 'Watering…' and was disabled, with no error shown. However, the 10 s timeout the reports expect is not in the request (which only asks for Water now, past-watering form, last-watered display, dashboard top 5 and a filtered list) and is not an app convention: composables/useApi.ts (useApiClient/useApiFetch) is unchanged by this diff (git diff main --stat does not list it), and neither the main branch nor the working tree contains any timeout/AbortSignal anywhere in frontend or backend. Every existing request (Add bed, Edit/Delete bed, plants, harvests, tasks) uses the same shared client and behaves the same way under a hanging API. The new watering calls follow the app's established request handling; the missing timeout is a pre-existing, app-wide trait, not a regression or an unmet requirement of this change.

watering-log/server-vs-client-date-timez.sentence: When the browser's time zone is ahead of the server's, a past watering dated with the form's default 'today' is refused as in the future, and 'Water now' stores a server-local date with a UTC time.
watering-log/server-vs-client-date-timez.evidence: Server clock: Thu 12 Nov 2026 14:42 CET (13:42 UTC). Opened a Playwright browser context with timezoneId Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14, local time Fri 13 Nov 03:42), signed in as the demo user, and went to /beds. Under 'Record past watering' for North bed, the date input defaulted to 2026-11-13 (max=2026-11-13, from todayIso()). I entered 2 litres and clicked 'Save watering'. POST /api/waterings {bed_id:1, watered_on:'2026-11-13', litres:2} returned 422 'Value error, Watering date cannot be in the future.' (schemas.py not_in_future compares against the server's date.today()). So the gardener cannot save today's date, which the form itself offers as the default and the maximum. Then I clicked 'Water now' for Shade corner. The response had watered_on '2026-11-12' (server-local date, from now.astimezone().date()) and watered_at '2026-11-12 13:44:10' (UTC). The beds page showed 'Last watered 13 Nov 2026, 03:44', so the stored day (12 Nov, which sorting uses) disagrees with the day shown to the gardener (13 Nov). Both parts of the report happened as described. Side effect: this test created watering id 3 for Shade corner.

watering-log/shared-watering-busy-state.sentence: On /beds, clicking 'Water now' on a second bed while the first request is pending uses one shared busy flag and message, re-enabling a pending bed's button (allowing duplicates) and overwriting the other bed's notice.
watering-log/shared-watering-busy-state.evidence: beds.vue has one wateringBedId ref plus single waterNotice/waterError refs. recordWatering sets wateringBedId = bed.id and clears both messages at the start, and sets wateringBedId = null in finally. In the running app (/beds, signed in as demo) I held all POST /api/waterings with page.route. I clicked 'Water now' on North bed: it showed 'Watering…' and was disabled. Then I clicked 'Water now' on Shade corner: North bed's button went straight back to 'Water now' and became enabled (Adis=false) while its POST was still held. I released Shade's POST: both buttons were enabled and only 'Watered Shade corner.' was shown. I clicked North bed again while its first POST was still held, which sent a 3rd POST. After releasing everything, GET /api/waterings showed two North bed waterings saved at the same second (ids 5 and 6, both 2026-11-12 13:36:18), so a real duplicate was recorded. At the end only 'Watered North bed.' was shown and Shade corner's success notice was gone. The single shared flag both re-enables a pending bed's button (allowing duplicate records) and overwrites the other bed's notice, as reported. I did not check the timeout claim in report 2.

watering-log/ssr-timestamp-timezone-hydr.sentence: Watering timestamps are formatted without a fixed time zone, so viewing the pages from a time zone different from the Nuxt server's causes SSR/client mismatches.
watering-log/ssr-timestamp-timezone-hydr.evidence: Code: frontend/app/utils/format.ts adds dateTimeFormatter (Intl.DateTimeFormat en-GB with hour/minute) with no timeZone option, while the existing date formatter pins timeZone 'UTC'. formatWatered/formatDateTime are rendered during SSR on /beds, / and /waterings (data comes from useFetch, with no ClientOnly wrapper). Repro: the Nuxt host is in CET. I opened a Playwright browser context with timezoneId Pacific/Auckland, signed in as demo@example.com, and clicked 'Water now' for North bed. On each of /beds, / and /waterings, the raw SSR HTML said '12 Nov 2026, 14:39' while the hydrated page said '13 Nov 2026, 02:39'. The console logged '[Vue warn]: Hydration text content mismatch ... rendered on server: 12 Nov 2026, 14:39 - expected on client: 13 Nov 2026, 02:39' and 'Hydration completed but contains mismatches.' on all three pages. So first paint shows the server's time zone (here a different calendar day too), then the text changes, and Vue reports hydration errors.

watering-log/stale-filter-results.sentence: On /waterings, rapidly changing or failing bed-filter refetches can leave a previous bed's rows displayed under the new filter or alongside the error.
watering-log/stale-filter-results.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /waterings (beds: 1 North bed, 2 Shade corner). I drove the filter with Playwright and used page.route to fail, delay or hang requests. (1) North bed loaded, then the Shade corner request returned 500: the alert 'boom' appeared and the table was gone (0 rows, empty count). Nuxt useFetch clears data on error, so the previous bed's rows do not render next to the error. (2) The same test with a network abort showed 'Could not load waterings.' and 0 rows. (3) The North bed response was delayed 3s, then I switched to Shade corner after 200ms: only the Shade corner row showed, before and after the late North response would have arrived. The late answer did not overwrite the newer one, because useFetch cancels or ignores the superseded request. (4) North bed slow-failed (500 after 2.5s) after I had switched to Shade corner: Shade corner stayed shown with no error. (5) Rapid toggling 1->2->1->2 with bed 2 failing: only the error was shown, no rows. The only stale display I found was while a request was still pending or hung: the previous bed's rows stay visible together with 'Loading waterings…'. That is a normal keep-showing-while-loading state with a loading indicator, not the reported problem of rows next to an error or a late answer replacing newer results.

watering-log/tasks-upcoming-error-no-ret.sentence: On /, when GET /api/tasks/upcoming fails (500, 400, reset, 429), there is no way to retry without a page reload.
watering-log/tasks-upcoming-error-no-ret.evidence: Reproduced the symptom: signed in as the demo user, opened /beds, routed GET /api/tasks/upcoming to a 500, then went to the dashboard using the in-app link. The 'Upcoming tasks' section showed the error text ('boom') and there was no retry control (no buttons in the section or in main). After removing the route, the section kept showing the error until I left the page. Going to /beds and back through the nav links (no reload) refetched the data and the section recovered ('No upcoming tasks'). So the claim 'no way to retry without a reload' is overstated. More importantly, the change did not touch this behaviour. `git diff main -- frontend/app/pages/index.vue` shows the tasks fetch, the tasksError AlertMessage and the missing retry are all unchanged from main. The diff only adds the waterings fetch and the 'Recent waterings' section. No page in the app has a retry control (AlertMessage has no action slot, and grep finds no retry handlers), so this is the app's existing error-display pattern, not something the watering change introduced or something the request asked for.

watering-log/tiny-litres-shown-as-zero.sentence: Recording a past watering with a tiny positive amount (e.g. 0.001 L) is accepted despite the 0.1 field minimum and is displayed as '0 L' in the notice, dashboard and waterings list.
watering-log/tiny-litres-shown-as-zero.evidence: Signed in as the demo user. On /beds I opened 'Record past watering' for North bed, typed 0.004 in Litres (the input has min=0.1 step=0.1, but the form is novalidate and the client only checks > 0), and saved. POST /api/waterings returned 201 with litres 0.004 (WateringIn only has gt=0). The notice said 'Recorded 0 L on 12 Nov 2026.', /waterings listed '12 Nov 2026  North bed  0 L', and the dashboard's Recent waterings showed '12 Nov 2026  North bed  0 L'. The cause is formatLitres using maximumFractionDigits: 2. So the stated 0.1 minimum is not enforced, and a recorded positive amount is shown as zero. I deleted the test row afterwards (DELETE returned 204).

watering-log/water-now-check-fails-after.sentence: After a reload of / or /waterings, the app check app-water-now-records-once fails, reporting zero POST /api/waterings sent where one was expected.
watering-log/water-now-check-fails-after.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, then reloaded / and /waterings. Neither page has a 'Water now' control (browser_find for /water now/i found nothing on /waterings; on / the only text matches are the nav link and an empty-state hint). That matches the request, which puts 'Water now' only on the beds page; the dashboard shows recent waterings and /waterings is a filterable list. So when the check runs on those pages there is nothing to click and 0 POSTs is the expected result, not an app failure. The 401/429 GET responses in the reports come from injected faults on the GET list, which has nothing to do with the POST. On /beds, clicking 'Water now North bed' sent exactly one POST /api/waterings, which returned 201 Created. The check was run on pages the feature is not meant to be on.

watering-log/watering-post-no-idempotenc.sentence: Retrying 'Water now' or 'Save watering' after a lost or timed-out response creates a duplicate watering because POST /api/waterings has no idempotency key or dedupe.
watering-log/watering-post-no-idempotenc.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour, but it isn't a defect. In Playwright I signed in and opened /beds. I routed POST /api/waterings so the request reached the server (route.fetch) but the browser got a network failure (route.abort). Clicking 'Water now' on North bed showed 'The garden server could not be reached.', but a row was still created (id 3). After removing the route I clicked again: the app said 'Watered North bed.' and created id 4 two seconds later, so North bed had two waterings. The code agrees: create_watering always INSERTs and the client sends no idempotency key. I don't count this as a defect for these reasons. (1) The request asked for none of this. It asks for 'Water now', a past-watering form, last-watered, a dashboard list and a filter page. (2) It matches the rest of the app. create_task, create_plant and create_harvest also INSERT unconditionally with no key, and the shared client has no timeout or idempotency anywhere. (3) Watering the same bed twice, even on the same day, is valid data, so the server cannot dedupe by content. (4) It is limited and easy to fix by hand: the button is disabled while a request is in flight, so normal double-clicks are blocked. A duplicate needs a lost response after the server succeeded, and then a manual retry. The waterings page has a Delete button for the extra row. I deleted my test rows 3 and 4 afterwards through the API.

watering-log/watering-saved-but-refresh-.sentence: On /beds, when POST /api/waterings succeeds but the follow-up GET /api/beds refresh fails, the save is reported as failed or the bed list is replaced by 'Could not load beds.', inviting a duplicate retry.
watering-log/watering-saved-but-refresh-.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /beds. GET /api/waterings returned 2 rows. In Playwright I made only GET **/api/beds* return 503 {"detail":"Service unavailable"}, then clicked the first 'Water now' (North bed). The POST went through: GET /api/waterings then returned 3 rows, the new one id 3, bed North bed, watered_at 2026-11-12 13:40:20. The page's main text became 'Beds / Add a bed ... Add bed / All beds / Service unavailable'. Every bed card was gone, the only button left was 'Add bed', and there was no 'Watered North bed.' message and no retry or reload control. Cause in the code (beds.vue recordWatering): after the POST it calls useFetch refresh(). refresh() does not throw; it sets loadError and clears beds, so the v-if on the bed list hides every card. The success notice (waterNotice), which belongs to a bed card, disappears with it. The user cannot tell the watering was saved and gets no way back except reloading the page. When the list comes back and they click again, a duplicate is recorded, since the POST has no dedupe. Variant not reproduced: the first report says the user would see 'Could not record the watering.' That did not happen here, because refresh() swallows the error. The user-facing defect (a saved watering with no confirmation, the list replaced by an error, and an invitation to retry and create a duplicate) is real.

watering-log/waterings-beds-error-silent.sentence: On /waterings, a failing GET /api/beds is ignored and the bed filter silently offers only 'All beds' with no error or retry.
watering-log/waterings-beds-error-silent.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, then used Playwright to make GET /api/beds return 500 and clicked through to /waterings in the browser. The network log shows GET /api/waterings 200 and GET /api/beds 500 (twice). The page listed 2 waterings (Shade corner, North bed), but the Bed select had only one option, 'All beds'. The page showed no error alert and no retry control. The cause is in waterings.vue: `const { data: beds } = bedsResult` never reads bedsResult.error, and the select loops over `beds ?? []`. So the user cannot filter by bed and is not told why, which looks the same as having no beds. Other load failures in the app do show an AlertMessage.

watering-log/waterings-load-error-no-ret.sentence: When GET /api/waterings fails, the /waterings page and the dashboard 'Recent waterings' section show only an error message with no Retry control, so recovery requires a reload.
watering-log/waterings-load-error-no-ret.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: signed in as the demo user, routed **/api/waterings* to a 500, then went to /waterings and / using in-app navigation. Both pages showed only an alert ('boom'), with no Retry button. The dashboard does not take `refresh` from the waterings fetch (index.vue:17). But this is how the whole app already handles load errors. On main, every load error is a bare AlertMessage with no retry: beds.vue 'Could not load beds.', plants/index.vue 'Could not load plants.', harvests/new.vue, and the dashboard's own summary and tasks sections. `git grep -i retry main -- frontend` finds nothing. The request did not ask for a retry control, and the new code copies the existing pattern exactly. A reload is not the only way back either: after removing the route, clicking 'All waterings' or the nav link refetched the list ('2 waterings, 14 L in total' with Delete buttons). On /waterings, changing the bed filter also refetches. A Retry button would be a nice improvement, but leaving it out matches the app's design and is not a regression from this change.

watering-log/waterings-navigation-blocke.sentence: Clicking the Waterings nav link while GET /api/waterings hangs leaves the previous page on screen indefinitely with no loading indication.
watering-log/waterings-navigation-blocke.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and loaded /beds. Then I routed **/api/waterings** so it never responds (1 request was caught) and clicked the 'Waterings' nav link. I checked at 0.5 s, 3 s and 12 s. Each time the address bar and document title had already changed to /waterings and 'Waterings · Garden Log', but <main> still showed the Beds page (h1 'Beds', bed cards, 'Water now' buttons). Nothing on the page showed a load in progress: no aria-busy, progressbar, status or NuxtLoadingIndicator element. app.vue renders <NuxtPage/> with no <NuxtLoadingIndicator/>. The cause is in pages/waterings.vue: `await Promise.all([useApiFetch('/waterings'), useApiFetch('/beds')])` at the top level of the page setup, which makes the client-side route change wait for the fetch. There is no timeout, so the page never renders and its error/Retry state is never reached. The user is left looking at the Beds page under a Waterings URL, with no feedback. Other pages (beds, tasks) use the same top-level-await pattern, which softens this a bit, but the new page still leaves the user stuck with misleading UI.

watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-ba.sentence: On /waterings, entering bad values into the 'Bed' filter select triggers the dev error overlay.
watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-ba.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /waterings (options: All beds, North bed=1, Shade corner=2). Picked the last option (Shade corner): URL became ?bed=2 and the list filtered. Picked the placeholder (All beds): URL went back to /waterings with 2 waterings shown. Neither produced an overlay. Then added bad option values to the Bed select and fired change events: 'abc', '999999', '-1', '<script>', '1.5'. Each time the page stayed up, with no Nuxt/Vite error overlay and no uncaught exception. The 422 responses showed inline as an alert (e.g. 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer...'), and the nonexistent id showed '0 waterings'. The only console errors were the browser's 'Failed to load resource 422' network messages. A full SSR load of /waterings?bed=abc also rendered the page with the inline alert and a Clear filter button (screenshot scratch/playwright/bed-abc.png). The code matches: useFetch errors go to wateringsError and render through AlertMessage, never thrown.

watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-be.sentence: On /waterings, when GET /api/beds returns malformed JSON or 500, an unhandled render error and dev error overlay appear.
watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-be.evidence: Signed in as demo user. With Playwright routes making GET /api/beds return 200 'malformed-json!' or 500 {"detail":"boom"}, I went to /waterings by clicking the client-side link from the dashboard (so the beds request ran in the browser, not cached). In both cases /waterings rendered normally: the filter showed only 'All beds', the watering list and total were correct, there was no Vue render error, no pageerror and no error overlay (only the expected 'Failed to load resource 500' network logs). The code explains this: waterings.vue uses `beds ?? []` in a v-for, so a null or string value can't throw. I also tried it from /beds: broke /api/beds, clicked 'Water now', then went to /waterings, and /waterings was still fine. The '[Vue warn] Unhandled error during execution of render function' the report quotes does happen, but on /beds: `TypeError: beds.value?.reduce is not a function` at pages/beds.vue, when the beds refresh after 'Water now' gets malformed JSON. That is a separate defect in the beds page, not the reported /waterings problem. Side effect: the test recorded one real 'Water now' watering for North bed (12 Nov 2026 14:42).

watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-ma.sentence: On /waterings, when GET /api/waterings returns malformed JSON, an unhandled render error or dev error overlay appears.
watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-ma.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, then used Playwright to route GET **/api/waterings* to a 200 application/json response with a truncated body ('{"broken": [1,2'), and clicked the 'Waterings' nav link (client-side navigation). Console showed '[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of render function at <Waterings ...>' and an uncaught pageerror 'waterings.value?.reduce is not a function'. The URL changed to /waterings but the page never rendered: the body still showed the Dashboard content (title 'Dashboard · Garden Log'), with no error message. Cause: ofetch/destr gives back the unparseable body as a raw string, so `waterings` is a string and nothing reports an error. The totalLitres computed in pages/waterings.vue calls waterings.value?.reduce, which assumes an array and throws during render. The app does not check the response shape, so the page crashes instead of showing its 'Could not load waterings.' alert.

watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-si.sentence: Reloading /waterings while signed out triggers the dev error overlay.
watering-log/waterings-uncaught-error-si.evidence: In Playwright: (1) cleared cookies and loaded/reloaded /waterings -> SSR global auth middleware redirected to /login?redirect=/waterings, login form shown, no error overlay, no pageerror. (2) Signed in, opened /waterings, cleared cookies, reloaded -> same clean redirect. (3) Signed in, opened /waterings, logged out via API but kept the stale garden_session cookie, reloaded -> clean redirect to login. (4) Reproduced the report's preamble: on /beds routed POST /api/waterings to 500 for a past watering (inline 'boom' error shown, handled), then went to /waterings, clicked Sign out, navigated to and reloaded /waterings -> clean redirect to /login?redirect=/waterings. No nuxt/vite error overlay element and no uncaught page errors in any run; the only console error was the 500 I injected myself. Code check: auth.global.ts runs before the page's top-level awaited useApiFetch calls, and loadCurrentUser catches failures and returns null.
